title: Star Trails Over Maunakea
caption: Star trails over Maunakea, Hawaiʻi

recognition.text: Published in the NSF NOIRLab image archive. No published rating.

story: Stars sweep across the sky as trails above Maunakea in Hawaiʻi in this classic star-trail photograph. The landscape below is lit by a first-quarter Moon, which stayed up for the whole time the pictures were being taken.

The trails were not captured in a single shot. More than 150 separate digital photographs, each lasting one minute, were stacked together in Photoshop, following a technique described in the March 2004 issue of Sky and Telescope magazine.

Stacking works because each short frame records the stars as small dots or short dashes in slightly different places. Layered together, those positions join up into continuous arcs. The arcs themselves come from Earth's rotation: as our planet turns, the whole sky appears to wheel slowly overhead, and a camera that stays fixed to the ground records that apparent motion as a streak of light for every star bright enough to register.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph made with a digital camera: over 150 one-minute exposures in visible light were stacked in Photoshop to build the trails.
understand.eye: The eye sees stars as fixed points at any moment; only by adding many exposures together does a photograph reveal their slow apparent motion as trails.

explore: The same set of images was also used to make a high-definition time-lapse movie, in which the individual frames are played in sequence so the sky can be seen turning.
alt: Star trails across the night sky above a moonlit landscape on Maunakea.
